key_insight: RESILAGENT proposes a three-pillar architecture that connects threat detection, simulation, decision-making and tamper-evident evidence for cyber-physical power-system resilience.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help power-system operators coordinate responses to combined cyberattacks, physical sabotage and extreme weather rather than relying on siloed monitoring.
method: Organize operations into Sensing & Data Intelligence, Resilience Analytics & Reporting, and Incident Response & Recovery.
Use a cloud orchestrator to coordinate agentic AI, multimodal models and real-time digital twins in a Detect–Simulate–Decide–Sign loop.
Anchor threat intelligence and CER/NIS2-aligned evidence on a permissioned blockchain.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes two operator threat scenarios and an IEEE-bus micro-benchmark covering false-data-injection detection, cyber-physical fusion lift, N-1 contingency screening and anchor cost, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: As a concept architecture, operational reliability and safe AI-guided response under real-world latency, data-quality and infrastructure constraints remain to be demonstrated.
paper_title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems
